I'll think through this year the way I always do — starting from what I did last year and what my neighbors around me are doing.

**Laying out the land.** I have 14 mu. The wheat-maize rotation is my main business — I'll put 10 mu on it, same plots rotating. Garlic is my cash earner near the village — I keep 2 mu for that because the price has been decent and my wife handles most of the planting. Cotton I keep 2 mu, mostly habit, though the returns are not what they used to be. My oldest son is away working in Shijiazhuang, so I cannot handle too much cotton picking.

**Wheat (10 mu, winter).** I always plant Jimai — the improved variety, seed from the county dealer. Last year I used about 20 kg urea and 50 kg diammonium phosphate per mu (roughly 18 kg N, 12 kg P₂O₅), that worked fine. This year fertilizer price is still high so I will keep it the same. I top-dress urea at jointing, another 10 kg. Potassium I add 5 kg per mu, my soil here is not too short on potash. I irrigate 3 times: before winter, at jointing, at grain filling. Spray pesticide 2 times — once for aphids, once for rust if I see it. Plough before sowing because I have wheat stubble to turn in. I expect around 500 kg/mu, same as last year.

**Maize (10 mu, summer) after wheat.** I plant Zhengdan or similar hybrid — hybrid is the only way now, traditional maize nobody plants anymore. No-till direct sowing right after wheat harvest, saves diesel and time. N about 22 kg/mu, split between base and big-bell stage. P 6 kg, K 6 kg. One irrigation if the rain does not come at tasseling. Two pesticide sprays — one for armyworm, one for borer. I expect 550 kg/mu.

**Cotton (2 mu, spring).** Improved variety, Bt cotton seed. Cotton needs more work — N about 16 kg/mu, P 8, K 10. Irrigate 3 times from the well. Cotton gets sprayed more — 4 times for bollworm, aphids, spider mites. Plough the field because cotton needs loose soil. Expect 230 kg lint per mu.

**Garlic (2 mu, winter, planted autumn).** Improved local variety from the market, I save some of my own bulbs too. Garlic is hungry — N 25 kg/mu, P 15, K 20. Irrigate 4 times, it cannot go dry. Spray 3 times for leaf blight and onion maggot. Rotary till the bed before planting. Expect 1600 kg/mu fresh.

decision.reasoning_summary: I keep 10 mu in wheat-maize rotation as my main food and grain income, 2 mu cotton out of habit and because the land suits it, and 2 mu garlic because my wife manages it and the price is worth the extra work. I mostly repeat what worked last year — improved wheat and hybrid maize from the dealer, Bt cotton, and my usual garlic. Fertilizer I keep close to last year's rates because prices are still high and I cannot afford to waste it, but I also will not cut so much that yield drops. I irrigate from my well when rain is short, and I spray only when I see the pest. With my son working off-farm I cannot handle too much labor-heavy cropping, so this split fits what my family can manage.
